comparisons.peer_topic: Interest Expense Variation and Debt Repayment
comparisons.peer_summary: Interest expense decreased to $92 million in 2024 from $106 million in 2023, primarily driven by the repayment of the 2.95% Senior Notes due in June 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their 2024 interest expense trends. Intel reports higher interest expense in 2024 driven by higher average borrowings. In contrast, AMD reports a decrease in interest expense ($14 million) to $92 million, driven by the repayment of senior notes. This highlights a divergence in capital management: Intel's debt load (and interest cost) increased, while AMD reduced its debt obligations.

sentences.text: In 2024, interest and other, net decreased primarily due to higher interest expense due to higher 2024 average borrowings and lower other, net.
Interest expense of $92 million in 2024 decreased by $14 million compared to $106 million in 2023, primarily due to repayment of the 2.95% Senior Notes due in June 2024.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest expense increase due to VMware Merger debt
comparisons.peer_summary: Interest expense increased to $3,953 million in fiscal year 2024 from $1,622 million in 2023, primarily due to interest on debt incurred for the VMware Merger.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose the primary drivers of their 2024 interest expense, but the drivers are opposite in nature: Intel's interest expense increased due to higher average borrowings (general debt load), whereas Broadcom's significant increase in interest expense ($1,622 million to $3,953 million) was specifically driven by debt incurred for the VMware Merger.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income (expense) deteriorated in 2024 compared to 2023 due to higher interest expenses from increased debt rates, partially offset by higher interest income from cash and investments; it had previously improved in 2023 due to higher rates on cash and investments despite higher debt balances.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Micron both explain changes in their net interest components for 2024. Intel reports a decrease in 'other, net' driven by a large derivative loss ($755 million) and an EC benefit, amid higher interest expense from borrowings. Micron reports that its net interest expense deteriorated in 2024 due to higher interest rates on debt, partially offset by higher interest income. While Intel highlights a specific non-interest 'other' loss, Micron focuses on the rate-driven cost of debt versus income from cash.

sentences.text: In 2024, interest and other, net decreased primarily due to higher interest expense due to higher 2024 average borrowings and lower other, net.

Included in other, net in 2024 is a loss of $755 million from the change in fair value of a non-designated derivative related to our assessed probability of paying construction-related liquidated damages to Apollo, our Ireland SCIP partner.

Interest Income (Expense), Net: Interest income (expense) deteriorated for 2024 as compared to 2023 primarily due to increases in interest expense as a result of higher interest rates on our debt, partially offset by increases in interest income due to higher interest rates on our cash and investments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Other Net Income Components and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Other, net includes realized or unrealized gains/losses from investments in non-affiliated entities and foreign currency impacts, with changes in fiscal year 2024 driven by valuation changes in those investments.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and NVIDIA both discuss the components of 'other, net' income/expense. Intel specifies that its 2024 'other, net' included a $755 million loss from a derivative related to liquidated damages with Apollo. NVIDIA describes 'other, net' as consisting of realized/unrealized gains/losses from investments in non-affiliated entities and foreign currency impacts, with changes driven by valuation. Both address non-operating investment or derivative impacts within this line item, though the specific instruments (derivative vs. equity investments) differ.

sentences.text: Included in other, net in 2024 is a loss of $755 million from the change in fair value of a non-designated derivative related to our assessed probability of paying construction-related liquidated damages to Apollo, our Ireland SCIP partner.
Other, net, consists of realized or unrealized gains and losses from investments in non-affiliated entities and the impact of changes in foreign currency rates.

comparisons.peer_topic: Investment and other income drivers in fiscal 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Investment and other income, net, increased by $613 million in fiscal 2024 compared to the prior year, primarily due to higher interest rates earned on higher balances of interest-bearing securities.
comparisons.comparison: Intel and Qualcomm both report on the composition of their 'other' income/expenses. Intel reports a $560 million benefit in 'other, net' from interest related to an EC competition matter. Qualcomm reports a $613 million increase in 'investment and other income, net' driven by higher interest rates on interest-bearing securities. Both companies highlight interest-related income as a key positive driver within their respective 'other' categories, contrasting with Intel's larger negative derivative impact.

sentences.text: In 2024, we also received and recognized $560 million as a benefit to other, net for interest in relation to the European Commission competition matter for which we recorded and paid a ruling amount to the European Commission in 2009 and that we were successful at challenging and overturning with the ruling amount refunded to us in 2022.

• Investment and other income, net increased by $613 million in fiscal 2024 compared to the prior year, primarily due to higher interest rates earned on higher balances of interest-bearing securities.
